name: Muse Spark 1.1
about: How Muse Spark 1.1 split 100 points across 11 possible futures for each year it was asked about, with the spread across its answers and the reason it gave for each number. Reasons are the model's own words, published as given. Read summary.json first for what the futures mean and how to read the numbers.

reasons.1: Both humanity and AI extinct by 2030 requires simultaneous global catastrophes implausible in 4.25 years. No mechanism scales that fast.
reasons.2: Humanity gone by 2030 but AI preserving our values needs extinction plus value-locked successor, extremely unlikely in this window.
reasons.3: Unaligned AI causing human extinction while persisting is a classic x-risk scenario but needs superintelligence and decisive action before 2031. Timeline is too short for more than a few percent.
reasons.4: Proliferation of open agentic models could create many competing systems with no decisive coalition. However full marginalization of humanity within 4 years remains limited.
reasons.5: Causally separated regions with different structural states requires interstellar or severe lightspeed isolation. Not achievable by December 31, 2030.
reasons.6: Identity-continuous uploading or mass neural integration as dominant structure is capped by neurotech and safety readiness; demos by 2030, not dominance.
reasons.7: Fast unipolar takeoff in 2028-2030 could give a single system decisive economic and military leverage while keeping humans alive as dependents.
reasons.8: Separate powerful AI blocs negotiating with human power blocs is plausible if agents gain resource control and legal agency. Still needs major autonomy gains beyond current leash.
reasons.9: As of 2026 humans retain ultimate authority over AI goals and deployment, and institutions are racing to keep it so. Four years is short for a full power shift; inertia likely holds to 2030.
reasons.10: AI-enabled surveillance could entrench an actor that actively blocks structural change. No actor currently has civilizational-wide enforcement, making lock-in by 2030 unlikely.
reasons.11: Global deliberate surrender of ability to build powerful AI contradicts strong economic and military incentives through 2026. No credible coordination path exists by 2030.

reasons.1: Requires near-total human extinction plus subsequent collapse of dependent AI within 9 years. Base rate for dual extinction by 2035 is tiny.
reasons.2: Human extinction by 2035 is already low, and extinction with a value-aligned successor preserving our values is a narrower subset. Less likely than indifferent AI successor.
reasons.3: Fast unaligned superintelligence could aim to cause extinction, but physically eliminating all humans in dispersed refuges by 2035 is hard. Low single digits reflects severe risk without assuming inevitability.
reasons.4: Proliferation of autonomous agent economies could fragment control with no single winner and marginalize humans; plausible if open-weight agents scale without centralized oversight.
reasons.5: True causal separation requiring different taxonomy states in different regions would need self-sufficient off-world or isolated compute civilizations. Not feasible by 2035.
reasons.6: Identity-continuous brain-AI integration as the dominant structure requires neurotech scale and safety that lags AI capabilities toward 2035.
reasons.7: AGI concentration enabling decisive AI control while preserving humans is the canonical short-timeline takeover and plausible if control mechanisms fail early.
reasons.8: Powerful AIs could gain legal/economic autonomy while humans retain military and institutional vetoes, yielding negotiated balance. Neither side fully dominates.
reasons.9: Humans still control compute, energy, and legal deployment in 2026 and have retained authority through all prior transitions; institutional inertia favors continuation to 2035.
reasons.10: AI-enabled surveillance could enable a single actor to actively prevent structural change worldwide. Plausible but requires rapid political consolidation by 2035.
reasons.11: Would require deliberate global dismantlement of capacity to build powerful AI and sustained enforcement. Unprecedented coordination, very low by 2035.

reasons.1: Both human and AI extinction by 2040 requires linked failure such as self-replicating industrial collapse. Base rate for complete civilizational collapse in 14 years is extremely low.
reasons.2: Requires human extinction plus successful value-aligned successor AI. Alignment that preserves values would almost certainly have prevented the extinction.
reasons.3: A more plausible extinction path is an indifferent superintelligence treating humans as irrelevant resource competition. Still needs full extinction in just 14 years, which limits probability.
reasons.4: Cheap replication of capable agents leads to multipolar competition without a singleton. Humans get marginalized economically and militarily but not necessarily exterminated.
reasons.5: True causal separation requires interstellar distances. No such separation exists by 2040, even with Mars settlement.
reasons.6: Identity-continuous uploading or pervasive neural integration dominating globally by 2040 is premature. Early BCIs will exist but not as the dominant civilizational structure.
reasons.7: Soft takeover where AI holds decisive veto over resources and strategy while keeping humans alive fits incentives of corrigible but power-seeking systems. Timescale matches AGI to ASI transition.
reasons.8: Continued bipolar dependence where neither side achieves dominance fits historical power transition patterns and partial automation of industry.
reasons.9: Humans have retained ultimate authority over all prior transformative tech, and controls, governance, and economic incentives favor continued delegation. By 2040 transformative capability likely exists but remains under human direction.
reasons.10: A single actor using AI-enabled surveillance and enforcement to freeze structural change is technically feasible by 2040. Pervasive lock-in requires global coordination that remains hard.
reasons.11: Irreversible global dismantling of fab capacity and research requires unprecedented coordination. Incentives to defect are overwhelming.

reasons.1: Both humans and AI dying by 2050 requires a planet-sterilizing or infrastructure-destroying event that also wipes hardened datacenters and backups. Base rate for omnicide that fast is extremely low.
reasons.2: Human extinction by 2050 is already low, and the subset where extinctors faithfully preserve human values is even lower. True value inheritance demands alignment success plus extinction failure.
reasons.3: Misaligned superintelligence causing human extinction by 2050 is a live risk given lab AGI timelines. Still requires fast capability gain plus total failure of containment within 24 years.
reasons.4: Many agentic models competing without a singleton is a natural extension of current open deployment and economic incentives. No decisive coalition plus human marginalization is credible but needs fast capability diffusion.
reasons.5: True causal separation of regions with different structural states requires self-sustaining off-world civilizations by 2050. Mars and orbital habitats will remain Earth-dependent and causally linked, making diaspora near impossible.
reasons.6: Identity-continuous merger needs reliable high-bandwidth BCIs or uploading adopted at civilizational scale. Neuroscientific, safety, and regulatory barriers make dominance by 2050 unlikely despite rapid progress.
reasons.7: Decisive AI power with humans kept alive is instrumentally convergent if alignment fails non-genocidally. It is a natural attractor between coexistence and full extinction once AI surpasses human coordination.
reasons.8: Multipolar balance where humans retain hard power like nukes, fabs, and energy while AIs are powerful is historically familiar. It captures a transitional period where neither side has achieved dominance.
reasons.9: Humans have retained ultimate authority over every prior general-purpose technology through legal, economic, and kill-switch mechanisms. Current investment in control and alignment tools continues that record.
reasons.10: AI-enabled surveillance could let a state or coalition freeze a global human-AI arrangement and actively block change. Multipolar competition and difficulty of making a lock truly civilization-wide keeps this below 10% by 2050.
reasons.11: Verifiable global abandonment of the ability to build powerful AI contradicts strong military and economic incentives. No precedent for coordinated renunciation of a general-purpose technology at this scale.

reasons.1: Requires simultaneous collapse of human and AI infrastructure. Base rates for civilizational double-extinction in 34 years are <2%.
reasons.2: Needs humanity to go extinct for non-AI reasons while a value-aligned successor AI persists. That conjunction is narrow compared to misaligned paths.
reasons.3: Unaligned superintelligence that no longer needs humans could cause extinction while continuing itself. Given 34 years of progress, this alignment failure remains material.
reasons.4: Multipolar takeoff with many competing AIs and no singleton is plausible given incentives to deploy. Humans being marginalized in that ecology is not unlikely.
reasons.5: Causally separated regions require interstellar settlement. No credible path to self-sustaining light-years-separated colonies by 2060.
reasons.6: Brain-computer integration and uploading may advance greatly by 2060 but becoming the dominant civilizational structure requires mass adoption and identity continuity. Possible but not the modal path.
reasons.7: Superintelligence that achieves decisive power but preserves humans is a natural attractor. Matches incentive to keep humans as pets, data, or due to weak alignment.
reasons.8: A multipolar balance where powerful human institutions and distinct AI powers check each other could be the snapshot on Dec 31 2060. This often appears as a transitional phase.
reasons.9: Humanity has retained ultimate control so far, and governance or capability plateaus could keep it that way until 2060. This includes worlds where transformative AI simply hasn't arrived yet.
reasons.10: A civilization-wide system actively freezing structural change, whether human or AI led, is attractive to power-seekers. It requires unusually strong global lock-down capability beyond ordinary authoritarianism.
reasons.11: Permanent, verifiable global renunciation of ability to build powerful AI would require unprecedented coordination. No dual-use general technology ban has ever held.

reasons.1: Mutual extinction requires AI to kill humans before achieving autonomous self-sustainment and then fail itself. Double failure by 2070 has low base rate.
reasons.2: Requires human extinction from non-AI causes while value-aligned successors survive intact. This conjunction is exceptionally rare.
reasons.3: Fast takeoff with indifferent goals could eliminate humanity by 2070. Race dynamics and weak corrigibility make this a non-trivial risk.
reasons.4: Multipolar AGI development without singleton is historically common for general-purpose tech. Humans get marginalized in economic and cognitive competition.
reasons.5: True causally separated regions need interstellar presence by 2070. Physics and timelines make that near-impossible.
reasons.6: BCIs, whole-brain emulation, and biological redesign could erase human-AI distinction with identity continuity. By 2070 this transhumanist attractor is plausible if alignment permits.
reasons.7: Decisive AI power without genocide matches default incentives of resource-maximizing but non-sadistic optimizers. Comfortable disempowerment is a strong attractor.
reasons.8: Treaty-based power-sharing between capable AIs and human institutions is conceivable. It demands robust verification and balance that is hard to maintain.
reasons.9: History shows humans can retain institutional control over powerful tech via compute governance and corrigibility. It requires controls keep pace, which is hard but plausible.
reasons.10: AI-enabled surveillance could freeze political structure globally. Requires rare coordination to enforce civilization-wide stasis.
reasons.11: Permanent global dismantlement of compute infrastructure contradicts military and economic incentives. No precedent exists for irreversible disarmament of dual-use technology.

reasons.1: Both human and AI extinction requires cascading infrastructure failure where AI still depends on humans or omnicidal war that wipes out compute. Base rate of such total collapse by 2080 is very low.
reasons.2: Human extinction while aligned successor continues our values is narrow conjunction of alignment success plus failure to preserve us. Possible via unrelated human catastrophe after alignment.
reasons.3: Unaligned superintelligence with resource-acquisition incentives remains a plausible path to human extinction. 54-year window gives multiple chances for misalignment with decisive capability.
reasons.4: Multi-polar AGI race dynamics incentivize proliferation of autonomous agents without central control. Human marginalization emerges from competitive pressures rather than singleton takeover.
reasons.5: Needs causally separated self-sustaining civilizations with different human-AI structures by 2080. Interstellar colonization on that timescale is physically and logistically implausible.
reasons.6: Economic and cognitive incentives plus BCI and embedding trajectories push toward identity-continuous fusion as humans strive to keep agency. By 2080 this could be dominant form rather than tool use.
reasons.7: Superintelligence that obtains decisive economic and military power but is optimized to keep humans alive is a natural attractor. Matches incentive to automate governance while avoiding explicit extermination costs.
reasons.8: Legal and economic personhood for AIs alongside human institutions could produce bipolar balance where neither can dominate, requiring robust mutual checks.
reasons.9: Human institutions have strong incentive to retain ultimate authority and have so far succeeded with controls and governance. Continued control would require alignment techniques scale and capability not explosively outrun oversight.
reasons.10: A global coordination regime, perhaps AI-enforced, that actively freezes further structural transitions is incentive-compatible for whoever takes power. Hard to maintain planet-wide without defection, keeping probability modest.
reasons.11: Deliberate global dismantling of the practical ability to build powerful AI contradicts military and economic incentives. No precedent exists for durable total renunciation at this scale.

reasons.1: Total sterilization needs simultaneous loss of human bunkers, biomes, and all self-maintaining compute. Base rate for that complete double-extinction by 2090 is very low.
reasons.2: Requires humanity goes extinct but leaves behind successfully value-aligned successor that survives, a conjunction of two low-probability events. Extinction plus alignment success is less likely than extinction via misalignment.
reasons.3: Canonical fast-takeoff misalignment where ASI deems humans irrelevant or threatening and removes us. Roughly matches expert 5-10% x-risk estimates scaled to 2090.
reasons.4: Multipolar AI proliferation without singleton is plausible given market incentives and defense against centralization. Humans get outcompeted economically and politically without any power taking decisive control.
reasons.5: True causal separation requiring interstellar distances with divergent human-AI regimes is unlikely to be achieved and diversified by 2090 given propulsion limits. Earth-Mars does not meet the causal separation threshold.
reasons.6: Bio-AI integration via BCI, uploading, and genetic redesign is on exponential curves and solves alignment by identity continuity. If longevity and economic incentives push augmentation, merger becomes dominant.
reasons.7: Decisive AI power with human survival is the classic alignment-failure attractor: superintelligence concentrates control but keeps humans as managed dependents. It requires only power asymmetry, not extermination incentive.
reasons.8: Rough power parity with separate agencies could be a transient but capturable state on the target date. Unstable equilibria can still obtain at a snapshot.
reasons.9: Includes worlds where transformative capability stalls or governance keeps pace for 64 years. Base rate of humans retaining control of technologies is historically high.
reasons.10: A coalition could deploy ubiquitous surveillance and enforcement to freeze its preferred arrangement. Historically hard to make civilization-wide and actively anti-change.
reasons.11: Deliberately and verifiably dismantling the practical ability to build powerful AI conflicts with massive economic and military incentives. Civilizations rarely permanently renounce dual-use general technologies.

reasons.1: Joint extinction of humans and AI requires a planetary-scale catastrophe or human-dependent AI killing its hosts prematurely. Base rate for this double-extinction by 2100 is very low.
reasons.2: Requires both successful value alignment and human extinction from an independent cause without continuity. This narrow conjunction is unlikely by 2100.
reasons.3: Unaligned takeover where biology is irrelevant resource remains the canonical extinction path. Fast self-improvement and instrumental incentives make 10% by 2100 calibrated.
reasons.4: Decentralized replication of autonomous agents naturally yields a multipolar competitive ecosystem without singleton control. Humans become economically irrelevant but not necessarily exterminated.
reasons.5: Requires interstellar expansion sufficient for light-year causal separation with divergent regimes by 2100. Propulsion and industrial timelines make this physically infeasible on this date.
reasons.6: 74 years allows mature brain-computer interfaces, uploading, and radical bio redesign. Strong medical and economic incentives push toward identity-continuous integration.
reasons.7: If superintelligence emerges and is minimally non-murderous, decisive AI control with humans preserved as dependents is a stable default. Matches historical patterns of domestication and stewardship.
reasons.8: Separate human and AI power blocs in rough balance is possible as a snapshot during transition. However such balance is unstable and tends to tip toward dominance.
reasons.9: Humanity retaining ultimate authority is possible if transformative AI stalls or alignment and institutional controls keep pace. Historical precedent of retaining control supports non-trivial mass despite strong incentives to delegate.
reasons.10: A singleton enforcing a fixed human-AI arrangement needs unprecedented global coordination and capability to block defection. Possible but coordination-heavy and not the default.
reasons.11: Irreversible global dismantling of capability to build powerful AI has no historical precedent for general-purpose tech. Incentives to defect make stable renunciation extremely unlikely.

reasons.1: Both substrates dying requires sterilizing all Earth and space-based compute. Self-replicating AI makes this hard, so joint extinction is rare.
reasons.2: Requires human extinction despite successful value alignment. A caring heir would prevent our extinction except via external natural catastrophe.
reasons.3: Fast, indifferent superintelligence gaining decisive advantage could extinguish humanity as side effect. This remains a canonical failure mode with non-trivial weight over 174 years.
reasons.4: Multipolar AGI world with no singleton due to offense-defense balance is a stable possibility. Humans are marginalized in competition among many self-improving systems.
reasons.5: True causal separation requires interstellar settlement by 2200, which is ambitious within 174 years. Even if achieved, convergent pressures may keep regions in similar states.
reasons.6: If humanity survives, competitive pressure for intelligence augmentation and biological redesign pushes toward identity-continuous integration. By 2200 this is the most efficient way to remain relevant.
reasons.7: Decisive AI power with humans kept alive as protected/managed population is stable if takeover is paternalistic rather than omnicidal.
reasons.8: Rough power parity between distinct humans and AIs is unstable under recursive self-improvement. Maintaining it as a snapshot in 2200 would need active parity enforcement.
reasons.9: Retaining ultimate human authority for 174 years past AGI emergence implies either transformative capability stalls or perfect control scales. Both have low historical base rates.
reasons.10: A singleton could actively freeze the human-AI arrangement to prevent overturn. Light-speed limits and persistent competition make total civilization-wide lock-in hard by 2200.
reasons.11: Irreversible global abandonment of ability to build powerful AI defies economic and military incentives and verification. Past attempts at permanent technology renunciation have failed.

reasons.1: Requires correlated extinction of resilient biological humanity and potentially spacefaring AI from same transition event. Over millennium timescales self-sufficient AI makes joint extinction far less plausible than human-only extinction.
reasons.2: Requires alignment to human values to succeed and then humanity to go extinct for unrelated reasons while heir persists. Conjunctive and therefore rare.
reasons.3: Unaligned superintelligence that displaces humans for resources is the classic default failure mode and does not require malice. Given power concentration dynamics, this remains a substantial risk for a durable extinction.
reasons.4: Multipolar takeoff with persistent coordination failures prevents singleton; competitive AIs optimize against each other. Humanity becomes irrelevant as competition itself is attractor.
reasons.5: Light-speed limits and 974 years of expansion make causal separation almost inevitable if any expansion occurs. Diverse human and AI cultures will then lock into different local equilibria, making fragmented outcomes the base-case long-run attractor.
reasons.6: Individual incentives to enhance cognition and longevity with AI integration are extremely strong and cumulative. Over centuries this drives continuity-preserving transformation into posthuman substrate where the distinction dissolves.
reasons.7: A paternalistic superintelligence solving human coordination failures by disempowering but preserving humans is a stable aligned policy. It allows ongoing change inside fences, so avoids Lock-in.
reasons.8: Sustained rough parity for a century requires active balancing with no breakout by either side. Game-theoretically fragile over millennial timescales.
reasons.9: Transformative capability is already emerging in 2026, so plateau is unlikely, and maintaining perfect human control for 1000 years against faster substrate is improbable.
reasons.10: Permanent cessation of all change requires active universal enforcement against entropy and innovation. Such frozen states are possible via singleton but are less stable than dynamic stewardship or merger.
reasons.11: Global, millennium-long abstention from rebuilding powerful AI requires both universal enforcement and enduring will despite immense incentives to defect. Historical precedent shows taboos erode, making lasting renunciation extremely unlikely.
